### Changed
- **`valkey.valkey.auth.usersExistingSecretChecksum` is documented** (giantswarm/valkey-app#72, giantswarm/giantswarm-platform-manager#212). From valkey-app 0.1.5 the Valkey chart renders that value verbatim as the pod's `checksum/users-secret` annotation, so a password rotated in `usersExistingSecret` restarts the Valkey when the mark changes with it. The key passes through the open `valkey` block as it always did and this chart sets no default for it, so no installation's render changes; `components.valkey.versionRange` (`0.x`) picks the release up on its own, nothing is pinned. muster's own mark is giantswarm/muster#1315.
### Removed
- **Breaking:** **The `klausGateway` keys the Slack-only gateway ignores, the `/v1`, `/web` and `/cli/v1` prefixes of its route, and `components.klaus-gateway.versionRange` below `2.0.0`** (giantswarm/klaus-gateway#319, after giantswarm/agent-platform#633). The meta chart no longer forwards `klausGateway.cli`, `klausGateway.lifecycle`, `klausGateway.upstream`, `klausGateway.agentgateway`, `klausGateway.routing.defaultTTL` and `klausGateway.a2a.saToken`: klaus-gateway 2.0.0 accepts them as no-ops and does nothing with them, and the connectivity chart drops the same six, which no template of it read. The component's range is `>=2.0.0 <3.0.0` and `examples/customer-bom.yaml` pins `2.0.0`, because the values this chart now sends do not start a 1.x gateway: it reads `lifecycle.driver`, and with none forwarded it falls back to `operator` with no `operatorMCPURL`. An installation that sets `components.klaus-gateway.versionRange` itself replaces the chart's range and nothing checks it, so **a pin below `2.0.0` has to move** — UPGRADE.md, "the `klausGateway` keys the Slack-only gateway ignores are no longer forwarded". The connectivity chart's klaus-gateway `HTTPRoute` publishes `/channels/slack` alone — `/v1`, `/web` and `/cli/v1` answer 404 on 2.x — and, having nothing else to publish, renders only while `klausGateway.slack.enabled`; the OBO route (`/auth/slack/`, `/connectors/complete`) is unchanged. An installation that still sets one of the six keys in its own values keeps forwarding it, harmlessly, until that values file drops it.
